Revisionary design passes mid-milestone
items.description:
Substrate primitive for re-running design (tdd-design) over an existing project with corrective intent — for the case where a semantic gap surfaces mid-milestone and the design needs revision without wiping accumulated work.

VALIDATION5 SURFACED: sessions were designed as duration-based generic time-tracking, but the persona (Marcus, weightlifting) actually needs weight + reps + sets per exercise. The data model assumption was wrong, but it's already encoded across:
  - Feature 1's shipped schema/Pydantic models
  - Features 2-5's designed scopes
  - Contract Note 006 (session-http-contract-v1)
  - 21+ done tickets

The fix needs a "design revision pass" that:
  (a) reads existing artifacts as context (already supported via _format_existing_X_block framing)
  (b) operates against a corrective directive ("revise the session model to weightlifting semantics")
  (c) retracts stale features/tickets cleanly (THE GAP — features/tickets are additive; naive re-run produces duplicates)

TWO PATHS:
  1. DISCIPLINE: extend the corrective directive to be explicit about retract+replace. Brittle, relies on agent discipline.
  2. SUBSTRATE: add a `revise_features: [slug, ...]` directive field that marks features stale. M2/M3 see them as "do not preserve, replace or retract" and substrate enforces removal at meeting end — analogous to milestone_plan snapshot semantics (P18/0.7.0) but operator-driven rather than emergent.

Substrate route is cleaner; needed for the design-iteration cycle real teams hit.

ALSO IMPLIES: cross-feature revision (data model change cascades through already-shipped feature 1 implementation + still-designed features 2-5). The full revision sequence:
  1. Revisionary design pass → updated feature/ticket designs
  2. Implementation re-pass → schema migration + Pydantic model update for already-shipped code
  3. Forward implementation of remaining features against corrected model

PAPER RELEVANCE: this is exactly the iteration cycle real teams hit and would be a strong differentiator vs one-shot agentic demos. Worth its own section once shipped.

Defer until post-MVP demo + paper. Don't block validation5; ship as-designed first.

items.title: Feature-level implementation ordering + dependencies
items.description:
Features today are flat peers in the dashboard with no ordering signal or inter-feature dependency model. Operators have to infer the natural sequence (foundation → user-facing → cross-cutting → instrumentation) from feature names. Validation5 surfaced this: observability was the 3rd feature in the queue when it should logically be the 5th — it instruments code paths that don't exist yet for features 4 (auth) + 5 (sync). The operator footgun: queue features out of order, ship code that fails or fragments responsibility.

PROPOSED ADDITIONS TO FeaturePayload:
  - ``implementation_order: int | None`` — 1-indexed sequence position. M2 assigns; dashboard sorts by it (None last). No substrate enforcement — operator can override.
  - ``depends_on: list[str]`` — slugs of features this one structurally depends on. Dashboard disables Queue button until depends_on are verified (with override).

WORKFLOW UPDATES:
  - tdd-design.yaml M2 directive: teach Rabbit to assign implementation_order + depends_on during feature composition. Foundation features get order 1; user-facing capabilities ordered by dependency chain; cross-cutting infrastructure (observability, monitoring, etc.) gets the highest order with depends_on listing what they instrument.

DASHBOARD UPDATES:
  - Features pane sorts by implementation_order ascending.
  - Queue button shows tooltip + disabled state when unmet depends_on exists.
  - 'Queue anyway' override available for operators who explicitly want to defy the recommendation.

PAPER RELEVANCE: gives a concrete example of where the substrate currently relies on operator implicit knowledge and what the substrate-side fix looks like. Worth its own short section on 'feature-graph as architecture' once shipped.

Defer until post-MVP demo + paper. Don't block validation5 progress; ship as-designed. The existing flat-features UX is enough for a guided demo where the operator knows what to queue.

items.title: pytest_passes per-failure ticket synthesis
items.description:
Substrate gap surfaced by validation5 feature 3's M9 verify pass.

CURRENT BEHAVIOR: pytest_passes runs the test suite. When N tests fail, the check returns ok=False with one finding describing the failure in aggregate. _synthesize_followup_ticket_from_finding produces ONE ticket whose title and location reference the first failure (or some summary). Validation5 had 6 failing tests but only one synthesized ticket; the operator-visible granularity is "tests are failing" rather than "here are 6 specific test failures."

GAP: review-finding-to-ticket fidelity is too coarse for multi-failure runs. The Tweedles work the single ticket and run pytest themselves to see the full list — works in practice but loses the per-failure attribution + lifecycle (can't track which tests are fixed and which still fail individually). For a user-facing demo where the operator inspects the dashboard, "1 ticket with vague title" is less actionable than "6 tickets, one per failing test, each citing the test path + assertion."

PROPOSED SHAPE: extend check_pytest_passes (verification.py) to emit one ReviewFinding per failed test instead of one rollup finding. Each finding's location is the test path (tests/foo.py::test_bar), the quote is the assertion error, the concern is the test docstring (when present), the request is "Run pytest <path>::<test> locally and address the failure." Same shape as Caterpillar's M8 findings, just substrate-emitted.

Downstream: each finding synthesizes its own ticket per the existing _synthesize_followup_ticket_from_finding path. Tickets all source: review_synthesis so they skip tea-party (the failing test IS the spec). Each ticket closes independently when its specific test passes.

PAPER RELEVANCE: cleaner narrative for substrate decomposes failures into actionable work units. Aligns the build-check finding shape with Caterpillar's review-finding shape — operator sees consistent ticket granularity regardless of source.

BACKWARD COMPAT: existing single-rollup ticket behavior is acceptable for now (Tweedles still see full pytest output). This is a fidelity improvement, not a breaking change.

items.title: Cross-feature ticket consolidation phase (M3.75) — runs after all per-feature M3.5 instances complete; identifies near-duplicate tickets across features (same source requirements, similar slugs, overlapping descriptions) and consolidates to one ticket under the most-fitting feature with the others retracted. Surfaced from mvp-demo M1 design: three features all emitted variants of 'sqlite schema for notes + tags' tickets. Probably belongs as M4 in tdd-design and/or as a standalone phase in tdd-decompose.

discovery-existing workflow: probe a codebase to derive existing-state structural artifacts (existing_module, existing_capability, existing_pattern) before design phases. Substrate-equivalent of discovery.yaml but the interview subject is the codebase, not the operator. Sources: file traversal, dependency inspection, verify_imports-style probes, optional operator clarifications when ambiguity surfaces. Output feeds milestones-as-trajectory: operator marks 'we're at milestone N (everything to here exists in code), design milestone N+1' and the substrate scopes design/implementation to the delta.

Archaeology decision mode + agent role: who emits the structural understanding artifacts when discovery-existing runs. Cheshire Cat is the natural default by personality (system-coherence role). Open question: does this want its own guest cast — an archaeologist character whose characteristic failure mode is over-fitting a narrative to messy code (the inverse of Caterpillar's coherence-reading)? Decide as part of the phase. Decision mode needs a name (proposed: 'archaeology' or 'existing_state'), substrate primitive support (allowed_decisions guardrail), and a constitutional teaching block on what good archaeology looks like.

Convergence-failure detection: flag spec ambiguity when review-pass loops oscillate. Today the substrate happily runs review → implementation → review indefinitely as long as Caterpillar keeps finding things and the operator keeps queuing the resulting tickets. Mvp-demo M1 surfaced the failure mode: same 2 findings (DELETE shape + tag validation error shape) recurred across 5 consecutive review passes (~$11 burned) because Contract Note 001 + ADR-001 left the correct shape under-specified. Implementers oscillate between valid interpretations, Caterpillar rejects whichever's current, repeat. Detection heuristic: if the same finding-cluster (by location + concern fingerprint, not exact text) recurs in N consecutive review passes on the same feature, emit a 'spec_ambiguity' observation flagging the contract artifact(s) the findings cite, and pause the implementation loop pending operator disambiguation. Probably wants a TUI surface: 'feature X has been circling — review pass 5 surfaced findings substantially equivalent to passes 3+4. Likely contract ambiguity in <cited contract notes>.' Stops cost-burn on convergence failures and gives the operator a clear signal for where to intervene.

Detect environment-class verify failures and route to operator-attention, not implementation. Today when build_check (pytest_collects / pytest_passes / npm_build) fails, the substrate synthesizes a follow-up ticket and queues it as Tweedle implementation work. That's correct for code-class failures (missing imports, contract drift, runtime bugs) — but wrong for environment-class failures: missing dev dependencies in pyproject.toml, missing env vars, missing migrations, missing system packages, broken venv. The Tweedles can't honestly implement 'install fastapi as a dev dep' — that's operator/devops work — so they either burn budget refusing or write half-cooked attempts. Mvp-demo F2 surfaced the failure: pytest collection failed because fastapi wasn't in [project.dependencies], the substrate routed the fix as an implementation ticket, tweedledum + tweedledee correctly pushed back ('this is an environment setup task, not a code implementation task'), both meetings hit MEETING_BUDGET, and the loop didn't converge. Detection heuristic: parse the verify failure for tells — ModuleNotFoundError + missing-from-pyproject, missing env var references, schema-not-provisioned errors, etc. → emit operator_attention artifact instead of synthesizing an implementation ticket. TUI surface: dashboard shows 'F2 needs operator intervention: install fastapi as dev dep' with a one-line suggested command. Keeps the implementation pipeline scoped to code-class work and surfaces tooling/devops as the operator's lane.

Dashboard 'Re-design milestone' action analogous to 'Decompose tickets'. Today the dashboard's 'Design this milestone' CTA hides once stories/features exist for the milestone — assumes design is done or in-flight. But operators legitimately need to re-trigger design (substrate fix landed mid-milestone, killed-run partial output to recover from, scope-shift after operator review of generated stories, etc.). Mvp-demo M2 surfaced this: after killing a partial design run mid-M2 and shipping a substrate fix (existing-code awareness block), the only path to re-trigger was wiping all M2 artifacts manually. Should mirror the tdd-decompose pattern: a 'Re-design milestone' button on milestones with existing design artifacts; transitions all artifacts attributed to this milestone back to in_design state, then offers tdd-design run launcher pre-scoped to the milestone. Optionally a 'Preserve existing artifacts as input' toggle vs full reset.

Milestone-vs-code coherence review pass — M8 catches internal drift (code-vs-ticket, code-vs-contract) but not external drift (code-vs-milestone-spec). Mvp-demo M1 shipped with the schema using a single 'content' column when M1's done_when explicitly named 'id, title, body, tags' as separate columns. The drift originated at M3 decomposition (Rabbit collapsed title+body into content), propagated through Tweedles' implementation, and Caterpillar's M8 reviews never flagged it because Caterpillar reads code-against-tickets-and-contracts — and the tickets themselves had 'content' baked in. Drift was visible if you read milestone.md and src/backend/models.py side-by-side; invisible to the review loop that exists. New phase or build_check: 'milestone_satisfaction' check that diffs current code state against the active milestone's done_when bullets. Could run as part of M9 verify, or as a separate end-of-milestone gate. Tooling exists for this conceptually — Caterpillar could even do it with the right prompt, but the substrate currently doesn't feed milestone.md to M8's review seed pool as a primary input.

Trace and fix the M1 milestone deletion path. The mvp-demo pilot lost M1's milestone file twice without a clear deletion path: `_apply_milestone_plan_snapshot` empty-emission guard is in place and should prevent obvious cases, no retract on milestones fired, no MilestoneRegistry.delete_by_slug callers outside the dashboard ticket-prune path, and the BUDGET-outcome gating should prevent the phased snapshot from firing for non-COMPLETE meetings. Yet M1 disappeared from disk during M2 design runs both times (mtime evidence at start of M2 design, but no traceable code path). Possible suspects: phased snapshot firing during a different phase than expected, retract handler unlinking on a target_kind other than ticket (the scope guard only checks ticket retracts), MilestoneRegistry.write() rename path firing with a payload that matches a different guid + different slug. Add a tracing wrapper to MilestoneRegistry that logs every unlink + a SIGCHLD-style audit log for milestone file operations so the next repro is debuggable. Blocks the autonomous-pilot goal — recurring data loss is incompatible with Tier 2 autonomous.

Tier 2 autonomous pilot — run a complete greenfield project end-to-end (discovery → milestone-plan → tdd-design × N milestones → tdd-implement × N milestones → working demo) with the operator participating only as gate-approver, not as fixer. No hand-edits to milestone files, tickets, contracts, or artifacts. No killing wedged runs. No manual cleanup of partial state. The operator may queue runs from the dashboard and review/approve outputs at standard gates, but cannot fix substrate fights. The deliverable is the working app + the total spend + the measurement of where (if anywhere) intervention was needed. Paper-grade evidence: 'Wonderland can produce a working application autonomously, on Haiku-4.5, for $X in Y minutes.' Prerequisite: M1-deletion bug traced + at least 2 of the wedge-detection roadmap items (convergence-failure detection 73690727, env-class verify routing dc95169a) shipped.

Memory invalidation substrate primitive — agents need a mechanism to invalidate stale episodic memory when the substrate's own behavior changes. Mvp-demo M4 design wedged on a substrate issue that had already been fixed: agents had accumulated 291 utterances across previous design runs discussing 'v1-has-no-authentication is in M2 consumes but undecomposable.' The substrate fix (exempting scope/constraint kinds from realization check) silenced Dodo, but the agents pattern-matched on memory and re-derived the same wedge. Operator-side remediation required: surgical SQL DELETE of utterances matching wedge keywords across 8 agent databases. Tier 2 autonomous pilot can't tolerate that intervention. Proposals: (a) substrate-emitted 'memory invalidation' artifact that agents read on startup ('the issue you remember from rotations 3-25 has been fixed'); (b) decay or recency weighting in memory recall so older substrate-state observations weigh less than recent observations of current state; (c) agent-side guard directive 'if you detect you're pattern-matching on episodic memory, verify current substrate state and trust that over memory' — softer, easier to drift past. Belongs in p20 as a Tier 2 prerequisite.

Branch episodic memory at the design level (supersedes c54056b7 memory invalidation primitive). Architecture: each milestone's design pass gets its own branch of episodic memory rooted at a clean snapshot. Implementation passes branch from their milestone's design branch (potentially per-feature branches inside that). Wedge churn from one milestone's design doesn't bleed into siblings; the entire argument history of a wedge can be discarded by dropping the branch. On milestone closed, a consolidation step (Mock Turtle?) produces a 'milestone N summary' artifact at the project-level layer — captures conclusions without deliberation, so future branches see WHAT was built without inheriting argument churn. Surfaced from mvp-demo M4 design: aggressive memory wipe of wedge-related utterances also wiped useful history of M3's shipped feature, leading M4 design to re-create M3's markdown work. Memory-as-flat-log is the wrong abstraction for milestone-scoped reasoning. Branching gives clean boundaries that work with the existing milestones-as-trajectory ontology. Belongs in p20 as a Tier 2 prerequisite — possibly THE prerequisite, since it eliminates the operator-surgery need entirely. Supersedes c54056b7.

Add persona-anchoring framing to milestone-plan for Alice. The tdd-design entry meeting prepends a milestone-framing block that names the active persona (from seeded persona requirements). Milestone-plan has no equivalent — Alice participates as a support voice (Rabbit is primary_speaker) but has no explicit 'you are speaking for X' anchor. Surfaced in mvp-demo2 Tier 2 pilot: Alice consistently got confused about persona during milestone-plan, not an issue when running design passes directly against basic directives (which named the persona inline). Fix: prepend persona-anchoring block to milestone-plan convener directive — name the highest-confidence persona requirement from seeds, frame Alice's support role as 'reviewing through this persona's lens.' Small directive edit; substrate-side primitive would be _format_persona_anchor_block(runner) helper mirroring the existing seeded-personas pattern. Belongs in p20 follow-up work surfaced during the autonomous pilot.

Caterpillar M8 review: seed sibling-feature context so he can reason about gaps covered elsewhere. Today Caterpillar reviews one feature in isolation — sees its implementation, tickets, contracts, ADRs. Doesn't see sibling features (under the same milestone or adjacent ones) that might be responsible for filling the gap he's flagging. Result: false-positive findings of the shape 'this code doesn't handle X' when feature B is going to handle X. Substrate fix: seed M8's directive with a structured sibling-feature summary — for each non-current feature in the same milestone (and maybe future milestones), name its slug, kind, sources, and primary capability. Caterpillar's coherence-reading then covers the landscape, not just the slice. Mvp-demo2 Tier 2 pilot surfaced this as a pattern: Caterpillar flagged gaps that subsequent features were already designed to fill. Adjacent to but distinct from T-a6 (milestone-vs-code coherence detection): T-a6 finds gaps the code doesn't cover; this prevents false-positive gap flagging.

Comparative pilot experiment: design-all-first vs interleaved-by-milestone sequencing. Current pattern (interleaved): milestone-plan → design M1 → implement M1 → design M2 → implement M2 → ... → integration. Proposed alternative (design-all-first): milestone-plan → design ALL milestones → implement M1 → M2 → ... → integration. Run the same project (e.g., the notebook directive) both ways, compare cost / quality / wedge count / operator-intervention frequency. Hypothesis: design-all-first addresses b3f440c8 (Caterpillar sees full sibling-feature landscape during review) and gives cleaner cross-feature consolidation, but loses the iterative-discovery feedback loop where impl reveals design needs. Substrate implications: existing-code-awareness block (_format_existing_code_block) assumes interleaved flow — design pass for M_n+1 surfaces M_n's code; design-all-first means later milestones' design sees no impl code, only spec. Memory branching also less clean — concurrent per-milestone branches without intervening consolidation. Probably wants a workflow flag (Workflow.design_all_first: bool = false) that controls the dashboard's queue-batching behavior + the order tdd-design / tdd-implement fire in. Paper deliverable: A/B comparative cost + quality data for the two sequencings, with discussion of which pattern works better for which project shapes. Surfaced during mvp-demo2 Tier 2 pilot.

Add feature sequencing — Feature.depends_on: list[feature_slug] field. Currently features have no explicit dependency ordering — Rabbit emits them during M2 composition as a bag, operator picks queue order arbitrarily. Adding explicit dependency between features would: (1) force Rabbit during M2 composition to think about what each feature delivers + what enables it — the design pressure tightens scope per feature (constraints improve quality, same pattern as snapshot semantics + milestone scoping); (2) make implementation order substrate-decidable — no operator guesswork on which feature first; (3) extend existing-code-awareness block — design for feature N can see code from N's dependencies (which have already shipped); (4) partially resolve b3f440c8 — Caterpillar's M8 review could reason 'feature N depends on X which is shipped; that gap I'm flagging is covered there.' Substrate changes: FeaturePayload gets depends_on field, M2 composition directive teaches Rabbit to think about order, M3 decomposition + tdd-implement queue respect the dependency graph (topological sort), dashboard queue UI shows the dependency tree. Surfaced during mvp-demo2 Tier 2 pilot — operator observation that 'putting features in an order would as a byproduct result in more tightly designed features.'

Auto-synthesize default directive from active milestone scope when operator leaves directive blank. Today the directive is operator-stated free-text; blank means the only milestone signal is the _prepend_milestone_framing block at the entry meeting. Mvp-demo2 M2 design surfaced the gap: Alice drifted into M1-flavored stories (save flow, multi-tab edit) during M2 design because the per-run signal of 'you are designing M2 specifically' wasn't strong enough. Caterpillar got it right (search story) but Alice's persona-anchored design instinct pulled toward capture-flow without the milestone reminder. Proposal: when run_workflow fires with empty/whitespace directive AND an active milestone scope, synthesize one from milestone fields — goal + done_when + 'this milestone is about X, not Y (Y is sibling milestones' job)'. Substrate-side derivation, no operator burden. Operator can still override with explicit directive when they want. Connects to 79ef174a (persona-anchoring) and b3f440c8 (sibling-feature visibility) — all three are 'agents need stronger contextual signal per phase' in different shapes.

Extend cross-feature consolidation (T-a5) to dedup against SHIPPED features from prior milestones, not just current-design tickets. Today consolidate_cross_feature_duplicates clusters tickets by upstream-source set across features currently in design. Misses the case where the current design pass produces a feature that duplicates work in a shipped/verified feature from a prior milestone. Mvp-demo2 M2 design surfaced this: Rabbit composed a 'markdown rendered preview' feature during M2 design despite M1 having a fully-shipped frontend/src/MarkdownPreview.tsx component. The existing-code-awareness block surfaced the file but Rabbit interpreted it as 'might need extension' rather than 'already done.' Substrate fix: extend the consolidator to also consider features whose lifecycle state is VERIFIED in prior milestones, and flag current-design features that substantially overlap. Could either auto-abort the duplicate (aggressive) or emit an operator_attention artifact (conservative). Same shape as b3f440c8 but at the design layer (Rabbit composing) instead of the review layer (Caterpillar flagging).

Two-tier feature presentation in design context: passive 'already shipped' block + active seed pool. Mvp-demo2 surfaced the tradeoff: when _load_features filters by primary milestone (to prevent Rabbit debating prior-milestone features in M3 composition), Rabbit loses the 'what already exists' signal and overshoots into adjacent-milestone scope (composed tags/search features during M3 design despite M2 having shipped them). The two purposes were entangled in the original unfiltered design — preventing wedge vs preventing overshoot. Proposal: split into two presentation paths. (1) Active-milestone features: in the seed pool as agent-visible artifacts (composable, amendable). (2) Sibling-milestone features (especially VERIFIED ones from prior milestones): in a passive 'ALREADY SHIPPED, DO NOT REDESIGN' block in the framing — visible as context but NOT seeded as bus artifacts (no risk of debate). This restores the existing-features-block intent (slug-stability + overshoot prevention) without re-introducing the wedge-bait dynamic. Belongs to p20 follow-up work surfaced during the autonomous pilot.

Coverage check: recognize 'requirement realized by existing implementations' as a satisfaction path. Today the milestone_realization check only counts a requirement as realized when a NEW feature in this design pass sources stories realizing it. Doesn't recognize that prior-milestone implementations (verified features + shipped code) already satisfy a requirement. Mvp-demo2 M3 surfaced this: M3's consumes_requirements included 'five-minute-setup-acceptance-bar-clone-run-create-tag-search-persist-in-browser' (a validation criterion meant to verify the end-to-end flow works). The slug embeds capability names (tag, search, persist); Rabbit read it as 'I need to realize tag and search' and composed M2-overlapping features. The coverage check pressured this by flagging the requirement as unrealized. Fix shape: extend compute_unrealized_milestone_requirements to ALSO check whether any VERIFIED feature from prior milestones realizes the requirement via its source chain. If a prior shipped feature already realizes it, mark as satisfied — no pressure on Rabbit to compose again. Conceptually adjacent to 4a2597a4 (cross-feature consolidation aware of shipped features) — same gap class at a different substrate layer.

Feature derived-state misclassifies ABORTED tickets as in-progress, causing pipeline_runner to iterate features whose only activity was aborted work — surfaced in crm-demo M1 impl run where a leftover aborted ticket on RBAC caused the pipeline to also iterate RBAC alongside the user-queued sqlite-schema feature, AND M9 build_check fix tickets got mis-attributed to RBAC because it was the 'currently iterating' feature. Fix: feature_lifecycle's derived-state-from-ticket-rollup logic should treat ABORTED tickets identically to DONE for the 'is this feature still active?' question. The distinction (DONE = completed successfully, ABORTED = completed unsuccessfully) matters elsewhere but NOT for pipeline-active-state filtering. Tier 2 gate violation: the substrate auto-ran fix tickets in the same run without operator re-approval.

Feature .md file gets lost from disk while feature-states.jsonl ledger still tracks it through verified — surfaced on obol M3 design where M1 user-facing feature 'kohl-views-his-accounts-and-can-refresh-the-dashboard' had a complete state history (proposed → in_design → designed → verified) but the .md file was absent from .wonderland/features/. Downstream effect: M3 design caucus saw broken citations on Feature 002 that 'looked like' references to the missing M1 feature, looped on coherence-fix proposals for several turns. Class of bug: artifact-lifecycle desync between state ledger and the artifact file. Repro hypothesis: M2-run substrate mutation deleted or moved the file (maybe during retract path, maybe during a feature-rename, maybe during a wipe that should have been milestone-scoped). Investigation: scan obol pilot run logs from M2 for any delete/retract/rename ops against feature paths, identify which workflow surface lost the file.

Milestone-scope feature filter's defensive default leaks unattributable features into every downstream milestone — seeds_fallback._load_features line 88 has 'if primary is None or primary == scope.slug: in_scope.append(record)'. Features the Jaccard-overlap heuristic can't attribute (typically because their sources are phantom or malformed) fall into the None branch and stay in scope across ALL milestones. Observed on obol M3 design: M2's Feature 002 had two phantom story slugs in addition to three real M2 ones; the phantoms diluted Jaccard overlap, the feature became unattributable, it leaked into M3's composition seed pool, and the M3 caucus looped for several turns on coherence-fixing the phantom citations. Fix: change the defensive default from 'keep' to 'drop with operator-visible warning'. Broken-citation features are usually a substrate bug, not legitimate cross-milestone material — warn the operator at run start and drop from seed pool. Companion bug to d9c120d4 (lost feature .md file).

M2 composition meeting created Feature 002 with phantom story slugs in its Sources line — 'kohl-views-account-balances-in-the-tui-dashboard-and-manually-refreshes' and 'kohl-s-financial-data-persists-across-app-restarts-in-local-sqlite' don't match any story on disk. The actual M1 dashboard stories had different slugs (01KRYQ1F-kohl-manually-refreshes-account-balances-without-restarting-the-app, 01KRYQ2F-kohl-opens-the-dashboard-and-sees-his-accounts-with-current-balances). Class of bug: feature.sources written from agent free-text rather than resolved against the actual story registry slug, OR M2 substrate failed slug-stability tightening (T-v6) against in-process-design feature citations. Investigation: walk M2 obol run logs for the composition step that emitted Feature 002, identify whether the slugs Cat/Rabbit wrote were already wrong on emission or were corrupted in serialization.

Ticket .md Status field and ticket-states.jsonl ledger drift — pipeline_runner reads md .Status, dashboard/audit reads ledger, the two diverge silently. Observed on obol-demo2 M1 implementation: 12/12 tickets had md=open but ledger said various states (queued, done, no-record), so the pipeline kept iterating tickets the ledger considered done. The same shape as d9c120d4 (feature .md lost while state ledger tracks) but for tickets. Fix: pick ONE source of truth, propagate to the other on every transition. Probably: ledger is canonical (atomic JSONL append, never lost), md status field gets re-rendered on each transition.

M8 review accept-verdict bulk-marks unrelated queued tickets as done — observed on obol-demo2 at 15:36:46: a single review for 'database-schema-seeding-and-debt-paydown-calculation' caused 6+ tickets (including build-check-fix-tickets like test-failed-test-app-mounts) to all transition queued→in_progress→done at the same instant with note 'ticket was worked in this iteration but queue→in_progress hadn't fired yet'. The bug-fix work was NOT actually done (test_counter_increments_on_button_press stub test still in file). The substrate's accept-verdict consequence is sweeping every ticket in the iteration's scope to done regardless of whether each ticket was actually addressed by the review. Fix: scope accept-verdict's mark-done effect to ONLY tickets explicitly named in the review's target_files / sources, not the whole iteration.

M3 decomposition fires multiple times on the same feature producing overlapping/duplicate ticket batches — observed on obol-demo2 schema feature: 4 separate batches (01KS0D0G, 01KS0D0Y, 01KS0D30, plus follow-up batches) decomposed similar tickets with slightly different slugs. The substrate ran one batch but ignored others; operator had to manually identify+delete dupes. Fix: M3 should detect a feature already has tickets cited against it and either skip decomposition or merge into existing ticket set.

Feature state doesn't auto-transition designed→queued when fresh tickets queued — observed on obol-demo2 where both features stayed at 'designed' even after M3 decomposition created tickets needing pipeline pickup, and after M8 review synthesized follow-up tickets needing rerun. pipeline_runner's iterate_only_in_states:[queued,in_progress] filter then skips the feature entirely; queued tickets sit forever. Fix: on ticket-creation OR ticket-state-change-to-queued, auto-bump parent feature to queued (when feature is in 'designed' or terminal-but-with-pending-work states).

Decomposed tickets cite wrong parent feature — observed on obol-demo2: implement-budget-aggregation-contract and implement-debt-paydown-term-calculation tickets in batch 01KS0D0G cite 'financial-data-schema-and-initialization' (the schema feature) when their conceptual work belongs to 'budget-and-debt-calculation-contracts' (the budget/debt feature). They ran as part of schema feature's iteration. Same family as 9231bcd5 (phantom citations) but where the citation does resolve, just to the wrong artifact. Fix: M3 decomposition's per_item:feature loop should enforce that emitted ticket sources cite ONLY the current iteration's feature (or stories scoped to it), reject anything else as a citation error at write time.

Pipeline ticket-selection picks done tickets over queued tickets via an unidentified code path — observed on obol-demo2 M1 implementation: even with .md Status=done AND ticket-states ledger=done on 3 D0G tickets, AND 5 explicitly-queued tickets (operator-requeued D0Y + substrate-queued DR3 follow-ups) all citing the same parent feature, the run at 20260519T154744 iterated ONLY the 3 done tickets through tea-party + implementation. The expected lane filter at workflow.py:1995-2006 (explicitly_queued wins when non-empty) should have produced the opposite behavior. Investigation: trace _collect_per_item_items invocation chain in the pipeline path for tdd-implement; check whether bus utterances at run-start are pre-loading the done tickets and bypassing the disk-fallback+state-filter path; check whether _ticket_to_feature_map's first-match-wins gives a different feature attribution than expected. Pairs with 85aaee91 (md/ledger drift) and 676a4da8 (bulk auto-complete on accept verdict) — same family of multi-source-of-truth bugs in the iteration layer. NOT REPRODUCED with a minimal test case yet; the obol-demo2 .wonderland/ state is the only known repro corpus.

Feature stuck at QUEUED derived-state when review-pass has no ticket-worthy findings — operator-observed pattern: Cat reviews, has no findings worth synthesizing as follow-up tickets, and queued tickets from the iteration don't advance to DONE so the feature can't derive to READY_FOR_REVIEW. Hypothesis after 676a4da8 fix: accept-verdict path now only advances IN_PROGRESS tickets to DONE (correct, prevents bulk-mark bug), but review-spawned tickets that were queued and never picked up by another M6 cycle stay QUEUED indefinitely. _derive_post_ticket_state then lands on QUEUED (any queued, none active → QUEUED). Operator notes haven't yet confirmed whether original feature-generated tickets are affected the same way (probably not, those enter via per-ticket meeting orchestrator that reliably transitions QUEUED→IN_PROGRESS at M6 entry). Investigation: confirm scenario with a single-pass feature, identify whether the wedge is mid-iteration (m7→m8 before tickets advance) or between-runs (synthesized followups queued + no next run). Fix candidates: (a) auto-DONE queued tickets that were synthesized in the same review-pass with no follow-up work pending, (b) auto-launch a sub-iteration for review-spawned tickets if no other findings need triage, (c) lower bar on derived READY_FOR_REVIEW to allow stray-queued-tickets when they're labeled as follow-up-pending. Companion to 5fe6acd1 (feature state auto-transition designed→queued) — same family of state-derivation lifecycle bugs.
Milestone over-coverage gate — story.realizes ⊆ milestone.consumes
items.description:
milestone-plan currently gates UNDER-coverage (a required requirement has no story) but not OVER-coverage (a story realizes requirements outside the milestone's consumes scope). Observed in mvp-demo2 baseline: M0 design produced user-facing stories that realized M1/M2 requirements, bleeding scope and forcing later milestones to either retread or under-design.

Gate: during milestone-plan finalization (and again during tdd-design seeding), assert each story's `realizes` set is a subset of the milestone's `consumes` set. Violations surface as a coverage_check failure — Alice/Caterpillar should either narrow the story's realizes list, retract the story, or escalate the milestone scope for revision.

Pairs with: existing requirement-coverage check (under-coverage), milestone-scope seed filter (34f37c9), retract substrate (T-m7).

Likely small diff — one additional check in the same code path as the requirement-coverage check.

items.title: Global Project registry overwrites project.yaml prime_directive — three-way sync bug
items.description:
Three storage locations for prime_directive get out of sync:

1. ~/.wonderland/projects.json (global Project registry) — captured at first-run by new_run.py:1059-1063
2. <project>/.wonderland/project.yaml prime_directive — captured at TUI run time
3. The directive text in the composer at run time

new_run.py:1092-1097 unidirectionally syncs (1) → (2) on every run when they differ. If a user runs a milestone-scoped directive once (e.g., 'Design milestone m1-foundation...'), the global registry captures it as the project's canonical prime_directive. Subsequent runs sync that milestone-scoped string INTO project.yaml, which agents then read as 'operator's original ask' — contaminating every milestone scope downstream.

Observed: mvp-demo-rerun-A's first run was M1-scoped; the registry captured 'Design milestone m1-foundation...' as prime_directive. Every subsequent M2/M3/M4 run had project.yaml silently rewritten to the M1 string, even after operator-side fixes to project.yaml. Required diagnostic to trace why the file kept reverting.

Fix options:

(a) prime_directive should be project-level, not run-level. Capture should fire only on project creation (skeleton apply / new-project flow), not on first-run.
(b) The sync direction should be project.yaml → registry, not the reverse (project.yaml is the source of truth, registry is a cache).
(c) Both: project-level capture + non-overwriting sync.

Related: this is the kind of bug that's invisible to the agents themselves (they read what the substrate gives them); only operator-side diagnosis surfaces it. Pairs with the citation-integrity / defensive-defaults memory note.

Affected files: src/wonderland/tui/screens/new_run.py:1051-1097, src/wonderland/project.py, src/wonderland/project_context.py

items.title: Milestone unlinking during tdd-design corrupts substrate state
items.description:
tdd-design runs are deleting milestone artifacts from disk, leaving downstream runs (esp. for that milestone's scope) without their structured constraint surface.

Symptom: observed on mvp-demo-rerun-A. After an M2 design pass that 'tried to fix a requirement,' the M1 milestone file (milestone-01KS0WPP-m1-foundation-data-layer-api-contract.md) disappeared from .wonderland/milestones/. Subsequent M1 design runs had empty milestone seed pools, fell back to project-level prime_directive, and designed for the full app surface.

Why it matters: with T-ab11 (milestone artifact seeded into every tdd-design meeting) and T-ab9 (filter to active scope), the milestone artifact is the load-bearing scope signal in design runs. Its disappearance silently disables the entire scope-discipline stack.

Known unlink paths in milestone.py:
1. _log_milestone_unlink + path.unlink() at milestone.py:436-444 — fires during MilestoneRegistry.write when slug changes. Logged.
2. workflow.py:5915-5934 'snapshot cleanup' — fires for milestone-plan workflow only. Logged.

Observed unlink was unlogged (no milestone-unlink.log on A). Likely cause: an agent used the write_file or delete_file tool to operate on .wonderland/milestones/ directly, bypassing the MilestoneRegistry.write path. The tool layer doesn't know about milestone-substrate semantics.

Compounding factor: tdd-design declares disallowed_decisions: [milestone_plan, ...] to block agents from emitting milestone_plan utterances during design — but the file-system tools (write_file, delete_file) are completely orthogonal to the speech_act layer. An agent that decides 'I'll just edit the milestone .md to fix this requirement' can do so freely.

Fix options:

(a) Path-level write guard: the file-tool layer refuses write_file / delete_file on .wonderland/milestones/ during runs (not just tdd-design — also tdd-implement, etc.) Milestones are operator-or-milestone-plan-only artifacts.
(b) Workflow-level disallowed_paths: tdd-design.yaml declares which paths agents can't touch with file tools. Parallel to disallowed_decisions.
(c) MilestoneRegistry.write rejects non-milestone-plan callers when called outside milestone-plan workflow context (active workflow check).

(a) is cheapest + most defensible. (b) is more flexible. Both reduce the same surface: agents inside design/impl workflows can't unilaterally modify substrate-of-record artifacts.

Pairs with: T-ab11 (seeding) which assumes milestones are on disk; T-ab9 (scope filter) which silently filters empty when no files exist.

Affected files: src/wonderland/tools.py (write_file / delete_file), src/wonderland/milestone.py (registry), src/wonderland/workflow.py (workflow-level guards).

items.title: Add foundation/capability axis to requirement kinds
items.description:
Observed in T-ab14 validator audit: existing milestones flagged false-positive because the requirement-kind taxonomy can't distinguish foundation-shaped from capability-shaped requirements of the same kind.

Examples:
- 'v1-success-criterion-persistence-contract-verified' is success_criterion + foundation-shaped (about infra deliverable). The T-ab14 validator treats all success_criterion as capability-indicator, so a foundation milestone consuming this fails the check.
- 'markdown-renderer-github-flavored-syntax-required' is integration + capability-shaped (the renderer enables user-visible behavior). The validator treats all integration as infra-appropriate, so a capability milestone consuming only this fails the check.
- 'developer-experience-and-onboarding' style milestones have developer-persona capability work; no requirement-kind currently distinguishes 'dev-experience capability' from 'user-experience capability.'

Proposal: add an orthogonal axis to requirement schema — foundation_or_capability (or similar name). Discovery's interview phase classifies each requirement on both axes:
- kind: persona / situation / scope / constraint / integration / stack_constraint / success_criterion / behavior / out_of_scope / deal_breaker (existing)
- axis: foundation / capability / both (new)

T-ab14 validator becomes more precise: flag based on axis, not on kind alone. Foundation milestones can consume foundation-axis success_criteria; capability milestones can consume capability-axis integration requirements.

Pairs with T-ab14 (milestone validator) and T-ab6 (milestone kind / roster filter). Same finding generalizes: the substrate's taxonomy is too flat — kinds describe shape (success_criterion / constraint / etc.) but not orientation (foundation / capability). Two-axis classification is the right semantic.

Affected: src/wonderland/requirement.py (add axis field), discovery interview prompts (capture axis at discovery time), src/wonderland/milestone.py:_validate_kind_consistency (consume axis instead of kind alone).

items.title: Registry rejections don't roll back bus utterances / memory
items.description:
When a registry write raises (T-ab14 milestone kind-consistency, T-ab15 requirement axis, T-ab18 feature cross-emission), the agent's upstream utterance is still recorded on the bus + in episodic memory. The artifact never lands on disk, but the agent's WORDS proposing it persist as recall context.

Observed: mvp-demo-rerun-A M3 design. Cat emitted features cross-tagged for M2 in a previous M3 run. T-ab18 correctly rejected the feature writes (artifacts didn't land), but Cat's M3 branch memory retained 131 utterances including a 'composing M2 features' emission. Next M3 design pass started → Cat read his branch memory → continued litigating M2 feature completeness instead of doing M3 work. Required manual M3 branch memory wipe (977 utterances total across 8 agents) to unblock.

Pattern: rejected emissions create CONTRADICTORY HISTORY for the agent. They said something; the substrate didn't accept it; next session they read their own statement as authoritative recall and continue from there. The agent's own past words become a wedge.

Two fix shapes:

(a) Transactional emission: agent emits → substrate validates against registries BEFORE bus publication → if rejected, the utterance never reaches bus or memory. Cleanest semantic but requires reordering the emission pipeline (currently emit → bus → registry; would become emit → validate → bus + registry atomically).

(b) Rejection-triggered retraction: when a registry write rejects, the substrate automatically emits a retract speech_act targeting the just-published utterance. Bus history shows 'agent said X then immediately retracted because substrate rejected.' Memory inheritance + recall logic already understands retracts. Smaller change but creates noisier transcripts.

(a) is the structurally right answer; (b) is the operationally cheap one. Either fixes the wedge.

Affects: src/wonderland/feature.py (T-ab18 raise path), src/wonderland/milestone.py (T-ab14 raise path), src/wonderland/interview.py (T-ab15 raise path), src/wonderland/agent.py / bus publication ordering.

Pairs with: project_attention_decay_through_workflow memory (which observed framing fades, but didn't catch the rejected-emission-persists-in-memory class of failure). Worth adding to that memory or making its own observation.

items.title: milestone-review workflow — cross-feature coherence within a milestone
items.description:
T-ab20 made M8 review scope-discipline-aware (per-feature, per-stack_span). That leaves a substrate gap: who reviews CROSS-FEATURE coherence within a milestone? An M2 capability milestone with 4 features (capture, edit-delete, markdown-preview, retrieval) needs a coherence check across all 4 — do they work together as a capture+retrieval flow? Currently no workflow fires for this.

Proposal: milestone-review workflow that fires after all features in a milestone reach verified state. Cat does the cross-feature coherence check at the milestone scope. Analogue of M5 contract-negotiation but at the milestone level: ''do these features actually compose into the milestone's promised deliverable?''

Workflow shape:
- Trigger: operator-launched, OR automatic when last feature in milestone hits verified
- Roster: caterpillar (+ maybe alice for persona grounding, queen for security pass)
- Meetings:
  - **M1 cross-feature coherence check** — Cat reads all features in milestone, their tickets, contracts, ADRs. Surfaces findings about cross-feature contract drift, missing integration points, persona-flow gaps.
  - **M2 verdict + retract** — Cat verdicts the milestone (approve / request-changes). request-changes spawns follow-up tickets attributed to the offending feature; approve transitions milestone state to shipped.
- Output: review artifacts at milestone-scope, possibly milestone-state transitions

Pairs with: T-ab20 (per-feature M8 review stays scoped), T-ab6 (milestone kind drives some behavior here too — foundation milestones may need different coherence checks than capability milestones).

Also adds the shipped milestone state to MilestoneStatus enum, complementing existing proposed / in_progress / done / deferred.

Roadmap as P3 because operationally the per-feature review usually catches enough; the cross-feature gap is currently absorbed by operator-discretion final checks. Worth doing for paper-grade rigor and to close the substrate's review-coverage loop.

items.title: T-ab23: verify dedup staleness — repeat verify findings on the same feature silently drop via _route_blocking_review's slug dedup. mvp-demo-rerun-A had 51+ build-check-verify-failed reviews resolve to 1 quiet ticket. Should at least bump ticket status to 'still failing after N attempts' or surface a count badge so the operator sees the rot.

T-ab24: TUI surface for operator-attention artifacts — env-class verify failures route to .wonderland/operator-attention/*.md but the dashboard has no render path. Operator only sees a stderr line that scrolls past. Need a card/panel in the project dashboard listing pending operator-attention items with the suggested command (uv add fastapi etc) inline.

T-ab31: discovery.yaml needs axis discrimination directive — pilot mvp-260522 had 17/23 requirements tagged 'both' (default) + 0 tagged 'foundation' because Alice has no constitutional or directive guidance for how to differentiate. T-ab15 shipped the axis schema field; T-ab31 ships the directive that teaches Alice to USE it. Persistence constraints, scale limits, consistency contracts should land as foundation-only; personas + situations on capability. Pattern after T-ab13's milestone-plan foundation/capability discipline section.

T-ab35: tool-level milestone scoping during scoping + composition phases — block read_file on cross-milestone stories/features/tickets when active scope is set AND the active phase is scoping/composition. Allow cross-scope reads of ADRs + milestone artifacts (legitimate foundation-context lookups). Don't apply to later phases (decomposition+, consolidation+, architecture, contract-negotiation, implement, review, verify) because by then per-feature iteration filters scope work naturally. obol-260522 M4 surfaced: 4 design reruns with empty memory + scoped framing all stalled because agents navigated to M0/M2/M3 artifacts via read_file and got drawn into cross-milestone coherence concerns. Substrate's tool layer is the last unaddressed scoping vector.

T-ab36: time-scope build_check fallback to current-run window — _pick_feature_for_build_check_attribution filters candidates to features whose latest state transition happened at or after run_started_at. Excludes operator-parked features (manual workarounds applied before run). Contextvar plumbing in telemetry.py + Runner.__init__; graceful degradation when filter empties a bucket.

T-ab37: time-scope IN_PROGRESS-counts-as-queued in feature-level gate — stale IN_PROGRESS tickets from prior interrupted runs were leaking features into new runs iteration. Mirror T-ab36 contextvar pattern; QUEUED stays time-independent (operator intent persists), IN_PROGRESS only counts when in-window.

T-ab38: dashboard Reset to pending button for stuck IN_PROGRESS tickets — operator-park affordance paired with T-ab37 gate filter. chain_transition walks IN_PROGRESS → QUEUED → PENDING. Replaces the operator workaround of moving feature to READY_FOR_REVIEW.

T-ab39: review phase memory_scope meeting_only + cycle-history seeds — M8 review is single biggest cost line in implement runs (/bin/bash.51-.75/feature observed on obol pilots). Apply T-ab25a memory_scope: meeting_only to drop cross-meeting deliberation chatter. Compensate for T-ab29 oscillation-detection signal loss by adding kinds:[review]/tail:2 to review meeting seeds.

T-ab40: decouple review-verdict routing from meeting outcome — extract _apply_review_verdict_routing from _apply_post_meeting_transitions so accept/blocking verdicts fire regardless of MEETING_BUDGET / MAX_ROTATIONS outcomes. Fixes long-standing tickets-stuck-IN_PROGRESS bug when M8 overruns its /bin/bash.60 budget after the verdict landed.

T-ab41: skip features with all-terminal tickets from implement lanes — feature-level gate admitted a feature in IN_PROGRESS lifecycle state even when all its tickets were DONE, burning M8 review budget on already-shipped work. obol-260522-1 schema-bootstrap burned /bin/bash.58 on review-only pass. Filter: features with any tickets but zero actionable tickets drop out; features with zero tickets at all still pass (T-ab16 compat).

T-ab42: dashboard markup escape + verify-attribution prefers lane feature — fixes MarkupError on verify tickets whose body embeds pytest traceback with literal [/b] markup, and routes verify-spawned tickets to the lane feature whose iteration triggered the verify pass rather than scattering across the project via highest-numbered-preferred-state heuristic.

T-ab43: post-meeting disk reconciliation for accept-verdict reviews — caterpillar wrote accept reviews to disk but bus utterances never landed, so _find_accept_review returned None and tickets stuck IN_PROGRESS. obol-260522-1 had 23 manual operator bulk-marks vs 0 accept-verdict completions despite 2 accept reviews on disk. Reconciliation scans .wonderland/reviews/ for verdict=accept records within meeting window when bus dispatch fires nothing.

T-ab44: set _current_meeting_id on phased meeting path — T-ab35 contextvar plumbing was only in _convene_one; tdd-design uses phased meetings via run_phased_meeting which never set the contextvar, so T-ab35 has been non-functional for design scoping+composition since it shipped. obol-260522-1 M5 design: 12 cross-milestone read_file calls all succeeded (M3+M4 stories+features), M5 produced 0 stories because agents focused on M3-M4 coherence. Fix: mirror set/reset around run_phased_meeting call.

T-ab45: scope-lock framing on scoping + composition directives — T-ab35/44 closed the tool layer but agents still reason cross-milestone via list_files / reviews / memory. obol-260522-1 M5: alice opened with Before I compose M4 and M5 features... — treated M4+M5 as one surface. Add hard-edge SCOPE LOCK prelude to composition convenor_directive AND synthesized milestone directive. Names specific drift patterns to avoid; tells cast to surface cross-milestone concerns as one sentence and move on.

T-ab46: filter list_files to active milestone in scoping/composition — T-ab35 blocks read_file but filenames themselves leak concepts via list_files. Agents see story-XXX-kohl-views-budget filename, reason already covered, skip generating fresh M5 stories. Extend scope-detection helper to list_files; hide cross-milestone artifact paths silently from listings during scoping/composition.

T-ab47: queue button treats QUEUED blocked_by deps as satisfied — dashboard _unsatisfied_blocked_by was only counting IN_PROGRESS+DONE as satisfied, forcing operators to wait an implement cycle before queueing dependents. Add QUEUED to satisfied set; substrate processes deps in order within same run.

T-ab48: StoryRegistry.write validates milestone matches active scope — alice in obol-260522-1 M6 design wrote 3 stories attributed to m5 (debt-tracking content correctly belonged to m5, but active scope was m6 csv-import). Substrate accepted whatever milestone alice declared. Reject mismatches at write time so alice retries with active scope.

T-ab49: single-agent phase succession requires ≥2 PASSED windows — when T-ab6 narrows cast to single agent (alice for capability scoping), all_passed_in_succession fired after 1 pass, collapsing max_rotations=3 + coverage_check into one shot. obol-260522-1 M6 scoping ended after alice s rejected T-ab48 emission. Fix: bump succession floor to max(2, cast_size).
T-ab74: content-level scope leak — ticket bodies describe cross-milestone work that structural gate (T-ab73) can't catch

T-ab75: operator-question cross-agent dedup — multiple agents (e.g. Rabbit + Caterpillar) independently fire the same/overlapping question_to_operator; each gets its own 600s timer + separate round-trip. Coalesce by content-similarity + broadcast the answer as shared meeting context so the second agent never re-asks.

T-ab76: auto-stamp feature.milestone = active scope when None at write time. Agents leave it None; substrate stays permissive; so T-ab73 ticket scope-lock AND T-ab74 content-leak gate both silently no-op (both resolve ticket->feature.milestone). Keystone fix makes the field reliable so both gates actually fire. Plus scope T-ab74 to active-milestone tickets (currently over-reaches across milestones, would retract prior milestones' tickets).

T-ab77: automated operator-question resolver (Tier-2 enabler). Intercept question_to_operator before the human round-trip; a cheap resolver agent answers from grounding context (active milestone goal+done_when, FULL roster for surface-ownership, directive scope-lock, consumed requirements, prior Q&A this run). Confidence-gate: answer autonomously when groundable in an artifact, escalate to operator ONLY for genuine forks (contradictory milestone / true product preference). Formalizes what I do manually. M2 receipt: all 6 operator questions were artifact-derivable, 0 genuine forks.

T-ab78: ticket->feature attribution breaks during multi-feature design — M2 produced 13 tickets but 5 cited the MILESTONE guid:slug as sources[0] instead of a feature, and the 3rd feature (geocoding-resolver) got 0 tickets (its work mis-attributed to the schema feature). Orphaned/mis-attributed tickets are invisible to cross-feature dedup (needs >=2 FEATURE parents), so it found 0 clusters despite obvious dups. The dedup is fine; its INPUT attribution is broken.
